title: How to Find Profitable Real Estate Deals in St. Louis MO (2024 Guide)
excerpt: St. Louis is one of the most investor-friendly cities in the Midwest, with low entry prices, strong rental demand, and plenty of distressed properties ripe for wholesale and flip deals. Learn which neighborhoods to target, what the numbers look like, and how out-of-state investors can break into this market.

sections.content: St. Louis, Missouri is quietly one of the best cities in the country for real estate investors. Home prices are well below the national average, rental demand is steady, and the inventory of distressed properties keeps deal flow strong for wholesalers and flippers alike. Whether you are just starting out — check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide for a solid foundation — or you are an experienced investor looking to diversify into a new market, St. Louis deserves a serious look in 2024.
St. Louis Real Estate Market Overview

The St. Louis metro area is home to roughly 2.8 million people, making it the 21st largest metro in the United States. The city proper sits in St. Louis County and the independent City of St. Louis, a unique split that investors need to understand when researching tax rates and comparable sales. The market has historically been a slow-and-steady performer rather than a boom-and-bust market, which is exactly what long-term investors want to see. Median home prices in the St. Louis metro sit around $230,000 as of mid-2024, compared to the national median of roughly $420,000. That affordability gap is the core reason so many out-of-state investors are paying close attention.
Average Home Prices by Area

items: City of St. Louis (distressed zip codes): $60,000 – $120,000
South St. Louis City (Bevo Mill, Dutchtown): $130,000 – $200,000

sections.content: This price range variety means investors at every budget level can find a strategy that works. A wholesaler can lock up a north St. Louis city property for $40,000 and assign it to a cash buyer for a $10,000 to $15,000 fee. A flipper can buy in South City for $100,000, put $50,000 into a renovation, and sell for $210,000 to $230,000. A buy-and-hold investor can purchase a duplex in Florissant for $175,000 and collect $1,400 to $1,600 per month per unit. The numbers work across multiple strategies, which is rare in most markets today.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in St. Louis
Top Wholesale and Flip Zones

For wholesale deals, North St. Louis City neighborhoods like Baden, Mark Twain, and Walnut Park offer some of the lowest acquisition costs in the region. These areas have high concentrations of absentee owners, tax-delinquent properties, and aging housing stock — all conditions that create motivated sellers. After-repair values (ARV) in these neighborhoods typically range from $80,000 to $130,000, which keeps deal sizes manageable and cash buyers plentiful. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly run comps and verify your numbers before making an offer.
Best Rental Property Neighborhoods

items: Florissant: Strong working-class rental demand, good schools, low vacancy rates
Lemay / Affton: Affordable duplexes and small multifamily, close to major employers
Dutchtown / Bevo Mill: Improving South City neighborhood with strong rental demand and rising values
Jennings / Pine Lawn: Very low purchase prices, high gross yields, requires strong property management
Clayton adjacent (University City, Maplewood): Higher price points but strong appreciation and low vacancy near Washington University

sections.content: Pro Tip: Focus on the 63116, 63109, and 63111 zip codes in South St. Louis City for flips. These neighborhoods have seen consistent year-over-year appreciation of 6% to 9%, strong buyer demand from young professionals, and enough distressed inventory to keep your pipeline full. Run every deal through our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to confirm your maximum allowable offer before you go under contract.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in St. Louis
Wholesale Deals

St. Louis is one of the most active wholesale markets in the Midwest. The city has a large inventory of vacant and distressed properties, many of which have been sitting for years due to absentee ownership, probate issues, or tax delinquency. A well-connected wholesaler can realistically close 4 to 8 deals per month in this market. Assignment fees typically range from $8,000 to $20,000 depending on the deal and the buyer pool. If you are new to wholesale, start with our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand the mechanics before you start making offers.
Fix and Flip Deals

Flipping houses in St. Louis is highly profitable when you buy right. Average renovation costs for a standard South City row house range from $35,000 to $65,000 depending on condition. Experienced flippers in this market are targeting a minimum profit of $30,000 per deal, with many hitting $50,000 to $70,000 on well-bought properties. The key is finding off-market deals before they hit the MLS. Read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) to learn the sourcing strategies that top St. Louis investors use every day.
Buy and Hold Rental Properties

The buy-and-hold strategy is where St. Louis truly shines for long-term wealth building. Gross rental yields in the 7% to 11% range are common in working-class neighborhoods, which is nearly impossible to find in coastal markets. Section 8 voucher holders are abundant, providing government-backed rental income for investors willing to manage lower-income properties. Single-family rentals in Florissant and Hazelwood are especially popular with out-of-state investors because they attract stable, long-term tenants and require less intensive management than inner-city properties.
Current Market Trends Investors Should Know

St. Louis has seen modest but consistent home price appreciation over the past three years, averaging around 5% to 7% annually in most target neighborhoods. Rising interest rates have slowed retail buyer demand slightly, which has actually increased the motivated seller pool — great news for investors. Population trends show slow decline in the city proper but strong growth in St. Charles County and outer suburbs, which is shifting where the best long-term appreciation plays are located. Industrial and logistics job growth along the I-70 corridor is driving rental demand in North County. Meanwhile, the ongoing revitalization of downtown and Midtown St. Louis is creating new flip and small multifamily opportunities that were not viable five years ago.

"St. Louis is the kind of market where a disciplined investor with $100,000 in capital can build a six-property rental portfolio in 24 months. The numbers still pencil here when they no longer make sense in Phoenix, Nashville, or Tampa." — Common sentiment among Midwest real estate investors at 2024 regional REI meetups
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Investing remotely in St. Louis is very doable, but it requires the right team and the right data. St. Louis is not a uniform market — a property three blocks from a great deal can be completely uninvestable. Understanding the hyper-local neighborhood dynamics is the single most important skill for an out-of-state buyer. Learn [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) so you can evaluate opportunities confidently without being on the ground every day.

items: Build a local team first: You need a boots-on-the-ground investor-friendly agent, a reliable property manager, and a licensed contractor before you close your first deal
Use crime and vacancy data: Tools like NeighborhoodScout and the St. Louis City open data portal give you block-level vacancy and crime statistics — use them
Visit before you buy: Plan one trip to St. Louis to drive target neighborhoods, meet your team in person, and get a feel for rental quality in your price range
Understand the city vs. county split: The City of St. Louis is an independent municipality separate from St. Louis County — this affects taxes, courts, and comparable sales data
Start with a turnkey or light rehab: Your first St. Louis deal should not be a full gut renovation managed remotely — build confidence with a cleaner property first
Join local REI groups: The St. Louis Real Estate Investors Association (REIA) and local BiggerPockets meetups are excellent ways to vet vendors and find off-market deals
Verify ARV with multiple sources: Never rely on a wholesaler's ARV — pull your own MLS comps, use our ARV Calculator, and confirm values with a local agent
